terms.comment: Quō īmus? — Cūr?: a small child’s travel questions.
evidence: Cic. Att. 16.6.2: cūr ego tēcum nōn sum?
Mart. 13.14.2: dīc mihi, cūr nostrās inchoat illa dapēs?
Catull. 85.1: quārē id faciam, fortasse requīris

terms.grammar: phrase: ob with the accusative of the relative

evidence: Ter. And. 979: Quid stās? quid cessās?
terms.comment: The impatient “why”: “what are you standing there for?”. Quid ita?, why so?

terms.gloss: why is it that …? what is the reason that …?
evidence: Cic. Cat. 1.6: etenim quid est, Catilīna, quod jam amplius exspectēs (Lewis & Short s.v. amplus)
terms.comment: Literally “what is there, that …”. Traupman gives the indicative; Cicero has the subjunctive when the question implies there is no reason.

terms.gloss: why? what for?; as a relative, and that is why
terms.comment: As a question it is the comic writers’ word (Lewis & Short: ante- and post-classical); as a relative, “for which reason”, it is Cicero’s too.

phrases.latin: cūr ego tēcum nōn sum? cūr ocellōs Ītaliae, vīllulās meās, nōn videō?
phrases.english: Why am I not with you? Why can’t I see the jewels of Italy, my little country houses?

phrases.latin: quid rīdēs? mūtātō nōmine dē tē fābula narrātur
phrases.english: why are you laughing? Change the name, and the story is about you

phrases.latin: clūdere quae cēnās lactūca solēbat avōrum, dīc mihi, cūr nostrās inchoat illa dapēs?
phrases.english: lettuce used to end our grandfathers’ dinners: tell me, why does it begin ours?

phrases.latin: ōdī et amō. quārē id faciam, fortasse requīris. nesciō, sed fierī sentiō et excrucior
phrases.english: I hate and I love. Why do I do it, perhaps you ask. I don’t know, but I feel it happening, and I am in torment

phrases.latin: Quāpropter, quaesō? — Quia ego hanc amō et haec mē amat.
phrases.english: Why, may I ask? — Because I love her and she loves me.

long-a.html: It is the ablative quā with propter after it, as the tmesis shows: quā mē propter addūxī (Ter. Hec. 3.3.4, as Lewis & Short cites it). Lewis & Short writes quā-rē for the same ablative, and in its own article prints Quāpropter? where it quotes Plaut. Most. 3.2.140.

sources: Lewis & Short: cur · Lewis & Short: quare · Lewis & Short: ob (quam ob rem) · Lewis & Short: quis · Lewis & Short: quapropter
The comment on cūr comes from the grouped card.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 111.
